mainTopic: Bedtime קריאת שמע, the protective power of תורה, and the meaning of suffering (יסורין של אהבה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching about saying קריאת שמע on your bed: a תלמיד חכם is exempt, but אביי says even he should say one verse of mercy, such as בידך אפקיד רוחי. Next come teachings of ריש לקיש: a four-step plan for beating the יצר הרע, and a reading of a פסוק showing that every part of תורה was given at סיני. רבי יצחק teaches that bedtime שמע is like a double-edged sword and keeps מזיקין away. ריש לקיש reads the same פסוק as saying that learning תורה keeps suffering away. רבי יוחנן objects that even children know this, and teaches instead that someone who can learn and does not is struck with ugly suffering. The גמרא then gives a guide for a person who suffers: check your deeds, then consider בטול תורה, and if neither fits, these are יסורין של אהבה. The אמוראים argue over how to define יסורין של אהבה. The גמרא proves that suffering cleanses sin, from a slave's tooth and eye and from the covenant of salt. רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that תורה, ארץ ישראל and עולם הבא all come through suffering. A new ברייתא about someone busy with תורה and kindness begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A Torah scholar is exempt from bedtime שמע
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous page's teaching: a תלמיד חכם does not need to say קריאת שמע on his bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is a Torah scholar, he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement that began on the previous page about saying קריאת שמע on one's bed. It adds that a תלמיד חכם is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching said everyone should say שמע on his bed. This line carves out an exception for a תלמיד חכם. The likely reason is that he is always busy with תורה and falls asleep thinking about it.

keyTerms.meaning: saying שמע on one's bed before sleep

phrases.english: If he is a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: This finishes a teaching from the previous page about saying שמע on your bed at night.

phrases.english: he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא אֵין צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the statement on bedtime שמע that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from saying קריאת שמע on his bed.

steps.title: אביי: even a scholar says one verse of mercy
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the exemption: even a תלמיד חכם must say at least one verse asking for mercy, such as בידך אפקיד רוחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even a Torah scholar needs to say one verse asking for mercy, such as: 'Into Your hand I entrust my spirit; You have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to the exemption just stated. A תלמיד חכם still has to say at least one short verse of prayer before sleeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption covers the full קריאת שמע, but it does not mean the scholar says nothing at all. אביי sets a minimum, which is one verse asking for mercy. He gives בידך אפקיד רוחי as his example.

keyTerms.meaning: Into Your hand I entrust my spirit

steps.whatToRemember: Even someone exempt from bedtime שמע should still say at least one verse of prayer, such as בידך אפקיד רוחי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for including בידך אפקיד רוחי in the bedtime שמע said today.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even a Torah scholar needs
to say one verse of mercy,
such as: 'Into Your hand I entrust my spirit;'
phrases.notes: תהלים 31:6

phrases.english: 'You have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי אַף תַּלְמִיד חָכָם מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the exemption given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a תלמיד חכם must say at least one verse of mercy before sleep.

steps.title: Four steps for defeating the evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches a step-by-step plan against the יצר הרע: stir up the יצר טוב, learn תורה, say קריאת שמע, and remember the day of death. Each step is drawn from a phrase in the פסוק רגזו ואל תחטאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: A person should always stir up his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says 'Tremble and do not sin.' If he wins, good. If not, he should learn תורה, as it says 'Say in your heart.' If he wins, good. If not, he should say שמע, as it says 'upon your bed.' If he wins, good. If not, he should remember the day of death, as it says 'and be still, Selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from ריש לקיש about fighting the יצר הרע. It is connected to bedtime שמע because the same פסוק mentions 'upon your bed.' He lays out four steps, each stronger than the one before, and finds each one in a phrase of a single פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan escalates. You move to the next step only if the one before did not work. First comes simply fighting back, then learning תורה, then קריאת שמע, which mentions accepting ה׳'s rule and reward and punishment, and last, remembering death. Every step is tied to the next phrase of תהלים 4:5, so the whole verse becomes one plan.
steps.whatToRemember: Against the יצר הרע: (1) fight it, (2) learn תורה, (3) say שמע, (4) remember the day of death. Each step is used only if the one before did not work.
steps.confusionAlert: All four steps come from ONE פסוק, תהלים 4:5. Each step is drawn from the next phrase of the same verse, not from four different verses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Chama said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
A person should always stir up
his good inclination against his evil inclination,
as it says: 'Tremble and do not sin.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 4:5

phrases.english: If he defeated it, good;
and if not, he should learn Torah,
as it says: 'Say in your heart.'
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: If he defeated it, good;
and if not, he should say Shema,
as it says: 'upon your bed.'
If he defeated it, good;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — יִזְכּוֹר לוֹ יוֹם הַמִּיתָה,
phrases.english: and if not, he should remind himself of the day of death,
as it says: 'and be still, Selah.'
phrases.notes: 'Be still' hints at the silence of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching brought in because it, too, links שמע to 'upon your bed.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fight the יצר הרע in four escalating steps: stir up the יצר טוב, learn תורה, say קריאת שמע, and remember the day of death.

steps.title: Every part of תורה was given to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching from ריש לקיש: each phrase of שמות 24:12 refers to a different part of תורה, which shows that all of them were given to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא also said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: What does the verse mean, 'And I will give you the tablets of stone, and the תורה, and the commandment, which I have written, to teach them'? 'Tablets' are the עשרת הדברות. 'תורה' is the written תורה. 'The commandment' is the משנה. 'Which I have written' is נביאים וכתובים. 'To teach them' is the תלמוד. This teaches that all of them were given to משה from סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same chain of rabbis. ריש לקיש explains a פסוק phrase by phrase, matching each phrase to a different part of תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists five things: לוחות, תורה, מצוה, אשר כתבתי, and להורותם. ריש לקיש matches each one to a part of תורה: the עשרת הדברות, מקרא, משנה, נביאים וכתובים, and תלמוד. His conclusion is that even the Oral Torah and the later books go back to what was given at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: what is meant by what is written

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש reads שמות 24:12 as showing that every layer of תורה, written and oral, was given to משה at סיני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that תורה שבעל פה goes back to סיני.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi bar Chama said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
What is meant by what is written:
'And I will give you the tablets of stone,'
phrases.notes: שמות 24:12

phrases.english: 'and the Torah and the commandment'
'which I have written, to teach them.'
'Tablets': these are the Ten Commandments;
'Torah': this is the written Torah;
'and the commandment': this is the Mishnah;
'which I have written': these are the Prophets and Writings;
'to teach them': this is the Talmud;
this teaches that all of them
were given to Moshe from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same chain of rabbis, brought right after the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every part of תורה, including משנה and תלמוד, was given to משה at סיני.

steps.title: Bedtime שמע is like a double-edged sword
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that whoever says קריאת שמע on his bed is like someone holding a double-edged sword, and he quotes a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Whoever says שמע on his bed, it is as if he holds a double-edged sword in his hand, as it says: 'High praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to bedtime שמע. רבי יצחק says it protects a person like a double-edged sword and brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The image is strong protection: a sword sharp on both sides. רבי יצחק's verse mentions praising ה׳ and holding a sword. However, the verse itself never mentions a bed or שמע, which sets up the next question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: Whoever says Shema on his bed,
it is as if he holds a sword
with two edges in his hand.
As it says: 'High praises of God are in their throats,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 149:6

phrases.english: 'and a double-edged sword in their hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main topic of bedtime שמע after the side teachings of ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying שמע on one's bed protects a person like a double-edged sword.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק's verse shows that it is talking about bedtime שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof. The verse mentions praise and a sword, but where does it say anything about a bed? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points to a gap in the proof. Nothing in תהלים 149:6 itself mentions lying down or שמע. The גמרא wants to know what links the verse to רבי יצחק's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: what shows this? how is this implied?

phrases.english: What shows this?
phrases.notes: How do we know this פסוק is talking about saying שמע on your bed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the link between רבי יצחק's verse and bedtime שמע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How תהלים 149:6 is connected to saying שמע on one's bed.

steps.title: The verse before mentions beds
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, or some say רב אשי, answers that the verse just before speaks of the pious singing on their beds, so the sword verse that follows refers to praise said in bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said, and some say it was רב אשי: From the beginning of the passage, as it is written: 'Let the pious rejoice in glory, let them sing joyfully upon their beds.' And it is written after it: 'High praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that we read the verse together with the one before it. The earlier verse mentions beds, so the praise and sword in the next verse are about praising ה׳ in bed, which is קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by context. Verse 5 sets the scene of the pious singing on their beds, and verse 6 continues the same scene with praise in their throats and a sword in their hands. Putting the two together completes רבי יצחק's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: from the beginning of the passage

steps.whatToRemember: The 'double-edged sword' verse is about bedtime שמע because the verse right before it speaks of singing 'upon their beds.'

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said,
and some say it was Rav Ashi:
From the beginning of the passage,
as it is written: 'Let the pious rejoice in glory,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 149:5

phrases.english: 'let them sing joyfully upon their beds.'
And it is written after it:
'High praises of God are in their throats,'
'and a double-edged sword in their hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי מֵרֵישָׁא דְעִנְיָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse before (תהלים 149:5) mentions singing 'upon their beds,' so the verse after it refers to praise said in bed, which is קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Bedtime שמע keeps harmful spirits away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that whoever says קריאת שמע on his bed is kept safe from מזיקין, and he reads a פסוק in איוב as a hint to this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק also said: Anyone who says שמע on his bed, harmful spirits stay away from him. The פסוק says, 'The sons of רשף fly high.' עוף (flying) means תורה, because the תורה flies away from you if you don't hold on to it. רשף means harmful spirits, because a פסוק lists רשף together with other kinds of harmful forces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יצחק about bedtime שמע: it protects a person from מזיקין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק decodes two words in the פסוק. עוף is read as תורה (the words of שמע), and רשף is read as מזיקין. Put together, the פסוק says that the תורה said in bed makes the מזיקין 'fly up' and away.

keyTerms.meaning: Harmful spirits; forces that can hurt a person
Stay away from him; keep their distance
A word in the פסוק read here as harmful spirits
Flying; read here as a hint to תורה
'This word means nothing other than'; a formula for decoding a word in a פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who reads Shema on his bed,
harmful spirits stay away from him.
As it says: "And the sons of reshef fly high."
phrases.notes: איוב 5:7. The plain meaning is sparks flying upward, but רבי יצחק will decode each word.

phrases.english: And "uf" (flying) means nothing other than Torah,
as it says: "Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:5. The word התעיף sounds like עוף, like something that flies away if you look away.

phrases.english: And "reshef" means nothing other than harmful spirits,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף וְקֶטֶב מְרִירִי״.
phrases.english: as it says: "Wasting of hunger, and devouring of reshef, and bitter destruction."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:24

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יצחק about bedtime שמע, following his 'double-edged sword' teaching from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying קריאת שמע on one's bed keeps מזיקין away, hinted in איוב 5:7.

steps.title: Learning תורה keeps suffering away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the same פסוק in a different way: whoever learns תורה is kept away from יסורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Anyone who learns תורה, suffering stays away from him. The פסוק says, 'The sons of רשף fly high.' עוף means תורה, as we just saw. But here רשף means suffering, because the פסוק puts רשף next to 'wasting of hunger,' which is a kind of suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש uses the very same פסוק, but decodes the word רשף differently, as יסורין instead of מזיקין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עוף still means תורה, just like for רבי יצחק. The only change is רשף: ריש לקיש reads it as suffering, since in דברים it stands next to hunger. So for him the lesson is about learning תורה in general, not only bedtime שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy learning תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Anyone who is busy with Torah,
suffering stays away from him,
as it says: "And the sons of reshef fly high."
And "uf" means nothing other than Torah,
as it says: "Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone."
And "reshef" means nothing other than suffering,
as it says: "Wasting of hunger, and devouring of reshef."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק used by רבי יצחק in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה keeps יסורין away, hinted in איוב 5:7.

steps.title: Even small children already know this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects to ריש לקיש: why decode a hard פסוק in איוב, when a clear פסוק in the תורה, known even to young students, already says this?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Even little schoolchildren know that! The תורה openly says: 'If you listen to the voice of ה׳ and keep His מצוות, all the sickness I put on מצרים I will not put on you, for I am ה׳ your healer.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש's teaching, saying it is too obvious to need a hidden hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that ריש לקיש is wrong, but that his point adds nothing. The idea that keeping the תורה protects from suffering is stated openly in שמות, a פסוק even children learn. So a hidden hint in איוב must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Young schoolchildren learning with a teacher
But look; introduces a point that undercuts what was just said

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying ריש לקיש's idea is false. He agrees that תורה protects; he is only saying it is too obvious to need the פסוק in איוב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
phrases.english: But even young schoolchildren
know this,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
phrases.english: as it says: "And He said: If you will surely listen to the voice of ה׳ your God,
phrases.notes: שמות 15:26

phrases.english: and do what is right in His eyes,
and listen to His commandments and keep all His laws,
all the sickness that I put on Egypt

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָשִׂים עָלֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ רוֹפְאֶךָ״.
phrases.english: I will not put on you, for I am ה׳ your healer."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָא אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's reading in step 9 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's teaching that learning תורה keeps יסורין away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An open פסוק in שמות already teaches that keeping the תורה protects from sickness, so the hidden hint in איוב cannot be coming to teach only that.

steps.title: Whoever could learn and does not is struck with ugly suffering
steps.stepSummary: Instead, רבי יוחנן teaches a new point: if someone is able to learn תורה and doesn't, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings on him ugly, troubling suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the new lesson is this: Anyone who is able to learn תורה but doesn't, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings on him ugly suffering that troubles him. The פסוק says, 'I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up.' 'Good' means תורה, as it says, 'For I gave you a good portion, My תורה; do not leave it.'
steps.whatsHappening: After his objection, רבי יוחנן gives the teaching he thinks is truly new: not learning when you can brings suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children's פסוק only says that keeping the תורה protects. רבי יוחנן adds the other side: holding back from learning, when you are able to, actively brings ugly suffering. He reads 'silent from good' as 'silent from תורה,' and 'my pain was stirred up' (נעכר) as the troubling suffering (עוכרין).
steps.whatToRemember: Learning תורה protects, as everyone knows; but רבי יוחנן adds that one who is able to learn and does not brings ugly suffering on himself.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Rather: anyone who is able to be busy with Torah
and does not do it,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings upon him
ugly suffering that troubles him,
as it says: "I was mute with silence, I was silent from good,
phrases.notes: תהלים 39:3

phrases.english: and my pain was stirred up."
phrases.notes: נעכר comes from the same root as עוכרין, the troubling suffering he just mentioned.

phrases.english: And "good" means nothing other than Torah,
as it says: "For I have given you a good portion,
phrases.notes: משלי 4:2

phrases.english: My Torah, do not leave it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting ריש לקיש's point as obvious in step 10, רבי יוחנן offers his own, new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is able to learn תורה and does not is struck by הקדוש ברוך הוא with ugly, troubling suffering.

steps.title: Unlike a human seller, ה׳ was happy to give the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, or some say רבי חנינא בר פפא, uses the פסוק 'כי לקח טוב' to contrast people with הקדוש ברוך הוא: a human seller is sad, but ה׳ was happy when He gave us the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא, or some say רבי חנינא בר פפא, said: Come and see how the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא is different from the way of people. Usually, when a person sells something to his friend, the seller is sad and the buyer is happy. But הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like that: He gave the תורה to ישראל and was happy, as it says, 'For I gave you a good purchase, My תורה; do not leave it.'
steps.whatsHappening: Picking up the פסוק just quoted, the גמרא brings a new teaching about how happy הקדוש ברוך הוא was to give us the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לקח means something 'taken,' like a purchase. ה׳ calls His own 'sale' good and praises it to the new owner, which shows He is glad to give it away. A human seller, by contrast, is sad to lose what he sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see; opens a lesson that points out something surprising
The way of flesh and blood, meaning human beings
Something taken; a purchase or acquisition

steps.whatToRemember: הקדוש ברוך הוא was joyful in giving us the תורה and calls it a 'good purchase,' so we should not leave it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:
a person sells an item to his friend,
the seller is sad, and the buyer is happy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not like that:
He gave the Torah to Israel and was happy,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם תּוֹרָתִי אַל תַּעֲזֹבוּ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "For I have given you a good portion (purchase), My Torah, do not leave it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by association: it builds on the פסוק 'כי לקח טוב' quoted at the end of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike a human seller who is sad, הקדוש ברוך הוא rejoiced when He gave the תורה to ישראל.

steps.title: When suffering comes, first check your actions, then consider neglect of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רב חסדא, teaches that a person who suffers should first examine his deeds. If he finds no sin, he should blame it on בטול תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא, and some say רב חסדא, said: If a person sees suffering coming upon him, he should examine his actions, as the פסוק says, 'Let us search our ways and examine them, and return to ה׳.' If he examined and found nothing wrong, he should attribute it to neglect of תורה learning, as the פסוק says, 'Happy is the man whom You, ה׳, afflict, and teach from Your תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about what a person should do when suffering comes. It gives the first two stages of a step-by-step guide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stage one: suffering is usually a signal to look at one's actions and do תשובה. Stage two: if he finds no sin, the cause may be not learning enough תורה, since the פסוק links ה׳'s afflicting a person with teaching him from His תורה. This connects back to רבי יוחנן's point in step 11 that not learning when you can brings suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: He should attribute it, hang the cause on

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Chisda:
If a person sees
that suffering is coming upon him —
he should examine his actions,
as it says: "Let us search our ways and examine them
and return to ה׳."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:40

phrases.english: If he examined and did not find —
phrases.notes: He means he found no sin that would explain this suffering.

phrases.english: he should attribute it to neglect of Torah learning,
as it says: "Happy is the man whom You, ה׳, afflict
and teach from Your Torah."
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא ואיתימא רב חסדא אם רואה אדם שיסורין באין עליו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the joy of giving תורה (step 12) to a new topic: how to understand suffering, building on step 11's link between neglecting תורה and suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suffering person should first examine his deeds; if he finds no sin, he should attribute it to בטול תורה.

steps.title: If no cause is found, these are sufferings of love
steps.stepSummary: The third stage of רבא's teaching: if the person checked for בטול תורה too and that is not the reason, his suffering is יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he attributed it to neglect of תורה and did not find that to be so, it is clear that these are sufferings of love, as the פסוק says, 'For whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's step-by-step guide. If neither sin nor neglect of תורה explains the suffering, it comes from ה׳'s love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new category: suffering that is not a punishment at all. The פסוק in משלי shows that ה׳ rebukes the people He loves, like a father with a son he cares for.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear, it is known for sure
Sufferings of love: suffering that is not a punishment but comes from ה׳'s love

steps.whatToRemember: The three stages: (1) check your actions, (2) consider בטול תורה, (3) if neither fits, these are יסורין של אהבה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not find' here does not mean he didn't search well. It means he truly was not lacking in תורה learning, so that cannot be the reason.

phrases.english: And if he attributed it and did not find —
phrases.notes: He tried blaming it on neglecting תורה, but he really was learning properly.

phrases.english: it is clear that these are sufferings of love,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "For whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:12

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם תלה ולא מצא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the third stage of the guide begun in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If neither sin nor בטול תורה explains the suffering, it is יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: ה׳ brings suffering on those He delights in
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב סחורה in the name of רב הונא teaches that whoever ה׳ delights in, He crushes with suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, who said in the name of רב הונא: Anyone whom הקדוש ברוך הוא delights in, He crushes with suffering, as the פסוק says, 'And ה׳ desired to crush him with sickness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching that supports the idea of יסורין של אהבה. It says that ה׳ brings suffering specifically on people He delights in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said some suffering comes from love; this goes further and says those ה׳ delights in are the ones who receive it. The proof is from ישעיהו, where the same verse joins ה׳'s desire with crushing a person by illness.

keyTerms.meaning: He crushes him, presses him down

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Sechora said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָפַץ בּוֹ —
phrases.english: Anyone in whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights —
He crushes him with suffering,
as it says: "And ה׳ desired to crush him with sickness."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 53:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא אמר רב סחורה אמר רב הונא כל שהקדוש ברוך הוא חפץ בו מדכאו ביסורין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching that strengthens the idea of יסורין של אהבה from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever ה׳ delights in, He afflicts with suffering.

steps.title: Does this apply even if he doesn't accept the suffering with love?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב הונא's teaching holds even for someone who does not accept his suffering lovingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be that this is true even if he did not accept the suffering with love?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to read רב הונא's teaching, that it applies to everyone who suffers. This is a setup line; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule sounded unlimited. The גמרא checks whether the person's attitude matters, preparing to show from the same פסוק that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it be? (a possible reading the גמרא is about to reject)

phrases.english: Could it be even if he did not accept them with love?

steps.triggerLanguage: יכול אפילו לא קבלם מאהבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of רב הונא's teaching from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the teaching applies even when the suffering is not accepted with love.

steps.title: Suffering must be accepted willingly, like a guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק continues 'if his soul makes itself an אשם'; just as an אשם is brought knowingly and willingly, the suffering must be accepted knowingly, with love.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'If his soul makes itself a guilt-offering.' Just as a guilt-offering is brought with awareness, so too suffering must be with awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the next words of the same פסוק in ישעיהו. Only someone who accepts his suffering willingly is the one ה׳ delights in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the suffering person to an אשם. An אשם is brought by choice, with knowledge, so the suffering must also be taken on with full awareness and acceptance. This limits רב הונא's rule to a person who accepts his יסורין with love.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the source that answers the question)

steps.whatToRemember: Suffering is a sign of ה׳'s delight only when the person accepts it with love, like an אשם that is brought willingly.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "If his soul makes itself a guilt-offering,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 53:10, the very next words of the פסוק quoted in the step before.

phrases.english: just as a guilt-offering is with awareness,
so too suffering — with awareness.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר אם תשים אשם נפשו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 from the continuation of the פסוק quoted in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; only suffering accepted knowingly and with love counts, learned from the comparison to an אשם.

steps.title: The reward for accepting suffering with love
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the פסוק shows that someone who accepts his suffering with love will see children, live long, and his Torah learning will last.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he accepted the suffering, what is his reward? "He will see children, he will live long." And more than that, his learning will stay with him, as it says: "And the will of ה׳ will succeed in his hand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק from ישעיהו to show what a person gains if he accepts his suffering with love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 used the first part of the פסוק to show that the suffering must be accepted willingly, like an אשם. Now the next words of that פסוק describe the reward: children and long life. The end of the פסוק adds one more reward: his Torah learning will last.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning stays with him and lasts

steps.whatToRemember: Accepting suffering with love brings three rewards: children, long life, and Torah learning that lasts.

phrases.english: And if he accepted them, what is his reward?
"He will see offspring, he will lengthen his days."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 53:10, the same פסוק as the previous step.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
his learning will last in his hand,
as it is said: "And the will of ה׳ will succeed in his hand."
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads "the will of ה׳" as the Torah he learns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם קִבְּלָם מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps reading the same פסוק used in step 17, now moving to its reward clauses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who accepts suffering with love is rewarded with children, long life, and lasting Torah learning.

steps.title: First view: suffering that does not stop Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about what counts as יסורין של אהבה. The first says it is any suffering that does not stop a person from learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי and רבי אחא בר חנינא argue about this. One said: Sufferings of love are any that do not cause a person to stop learning Torah, as it says: "Fortunate is the man whom You, God, make suffer, and teach him from Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens an argument about how to define יסורין של אהבה and gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said that suffering with no clear cause is יסורין של אהבה. Now one אמורא adds a limit: it only counts if the person can still learn Torah. His proof is the פסוק, which puts the suffering together with "teach him from Your Torah."
steps.confusionAlert: In step 13, בטול תורה was a sin that could cause suffering. Here it means something else: the suffering itself is so heavy that it stops him from learning.

phrases.english: They argue about it

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi and Rabbi Acha bar Chanina.
One said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't tell us which of the two said which opinion.

phrases.english: These are sufferings of love:
any that do not involve stopping Torah learning,
as it is said: "Fortunate is the man
whom You, God, make suffer, and teach him from Your Torah."
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:12

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question: what exactly is the definition of יסורין של אהבה?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יסורין של אהבה are only sufferings that do not stop Torah learning.

steps.title: Second view: suffering that does not stop תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says יסורין של אהבה are sufferings that do not stop a person from davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: Sufferings of love are any that do not cause a person to stop davening, as it says: "Blessed is God, Who did not take away my prayer or His kindness from me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the argument, with its own definition and its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is תפלה, not Torah: if the person can still daven, the suffering counts as love. The פסוק links God's kindness to the fact that He did not take away the speaker's prayer.

phrases.english: And one said:
These are sufferings of love:
any that do not involve stopping prayer,
as it is said: "Blessed is God

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא הֵסִיר תְּפִלָּתִי וְחַסְדּוֹ מֵאִתִּי״.
phrases.english: Who did not take away my prayer, nor His kindness from me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 66:20

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing definition in the same argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יסורין של אהבה are only sufferings that do not stop תפלה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds are sufferings of love
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא brings a teaching from רבי יוחנן, through his father, that even sufferings which stop Torah or תפלה are יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, the son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said to them: This is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Both of these are sufferings of love, as it says: "For the one whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes."
steps.whatsHappening: A third voice speaks to both sides of the argument and says that both kinds of suffering count as love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier opinion left something out: suffering that stops Torah, or suffering that stops תפלה. רבי יוחנן includes them both. His proof is a broad פסוק: whoever ה׳ loves, He rebukes, with no limit on what kind of suffering.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, suffering counts as יסורין של אהבה even if it stops a person from learning or davening.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to them,
the son of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said,
phrases.notes: He is quoting his own father here.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵן,
phrases.english: Both these and those are sufferings of love,
phrases.notes: "These and those" means suffering that stops Torah and suffering that stops תפלה.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "For the one whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both sides of the argument with a wider definition from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sufferings that stop Torah learning and sufferings that stop תפלה are both יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: What does 'from Your Torah You teach him' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second half of the פסוק, 'and from Your Torah You teach him,' means, if it is not talking about suffering that comes along with Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, then, does the פסוק mean when it says 'and from Your Torah You teach him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the end of the פסוק. It is setting up the next step, where it will explain these words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן just taught that even suffering which stops Torah learning can be יסורין של אהבה. But the פסוק seems to pair suffering with Torah learning, as if only suffering that still lets you learn counts. So the גמרא asks: if Torah learning is not the condition, what are those words doing in the פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: What, then, does the פסוק come to teach? It asks why a phrase is there.
'And from Your Torah You teach him' (the end of the פסוק)

phrases.english: What, then, does the verse mean when it says
"and from Your Torah You teach him"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוחנן's view fits the end of the פסוק he is relying on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'from Your Torah You teach him' mean, if Torah learning is not a condition for יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: Read it as 'You teach us'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the word as 'You teach us': the Torah teaches us this idea, that suffering is good for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't read it as 'You teach him.' Read it as 'You teach us.' This idea, You teach us from Your Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the word with different vowels. The פסוק is now saying that the Torah itself teaches us the value of suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the phrase is no longer a condition about the sufferer's learning. It points to a source: somewhere in the Torah we can learn that suffering helps a person. The next step shows where.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't read it as ... but rather as ... (a reading with changed vowels to bring out a lesson)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the גמרא is changing the פסוק. The plain reading stays. The גמרא is adding a second layer of meaning hidden in the same letters.

phrases.english: Do not read it as "You teach him,"
but rather "You teach us."
phrases.notes: The letters are the same; only the vowels change, turning 'him' into 'us.'

phrases.english: This idea, You teach us from Your Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ״, אֶלָּא תְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by rereading the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase means the Torah teaches us that suffering is beneficial. It is not a condition that the sufferer must keep learning.

steps.title: The proof from a slave's tooth and eye
steps.stepSummary: The Torah's source is a קל וחומר: if losing one limb frees a slave, suffering that affects the whole body surely frees a person from his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it with a קל וחומר from tooth and eye. A tooth or an eye is only one limb of a person, and still a slave goes free because of it. Sufferings scrub a person's whole body, so all the more so they free him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where in the Torah we learn that suffering helps a person. It uses the law of a slave who goes free if his master knocks out his tooth or eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a damaged tooth or eye wins a slave his freedom. Suffering touches the whole body, not just one limb. So it should surely bring a person 'freedom,' meaning cleansing from his sins.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one
tooth and eye; a slave goes free if his master destroys one of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the Torah source behind the whole idea of יסורין של אהבה: suffering is a way of being cleansed, not only a punishment.

phrases.english: It is learned through a kal vachomer from tooth and eye.
phrases.notes: שמות 21:26-27: a master who knocks out his slave's eye or tooth must set him free.

phrases.english: Just as a tooth or an eye,
which are only one of a person's limbs,
a slave goes free because of them,

phrases.aramaic: יִסּוּרִין שֶׁמְּמָרְקִין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: sufferings, which scrub a person's entire body,
all the more so.
phrases.notes: He means that all the more so they 'free' a person, from his sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִשֵּׁן וָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in which Torah teaching step 23 was pointing to.
steps.raayaObject: That suffering cleanses and frees a person from sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from the law that a slave goes free for a lost tooth or eye

steps.title: ריש לקיש: suffering is a covenant, like salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links this to ריש לקיש: the word 'covenant' appears with salt and with suffering. Salt sweetens meat, and suffering cleanses all of a person's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said. The word 'covenant' is used about salt, and 'covenant' is used about suffering. About salt it says 'Do not leave out the salt of the covenant.' About suffering it says 'These are the words of the covenant.' Just as salt sweetens meat, suffering cleanses all of a person's sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's teaching, which says the same thing in another way. It compares suffering to salt because the Torah calls both a 'covenant.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places links them. Salt makes raw meat good to eat, and in the same way suffering 'sweetens' a person by removing his sins. This backs up the idea from the slave law with a second source.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is the same as (a link to an earlier teaching)

phrases.english: And this is the teaching of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
"Covenant" is said about salt,
and "covenant" is said about suffering.
"Covenant" is said about salt, as it is written:
"Do not leave out the salt of the covenant."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

phrases.english: And "covenant" is said about suffering, as it is written:
"These are the words of the covenant."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:69. It comes right after the long list of curses and sufferings, so it is read as being about them.

phrases.english: Just as with the "covenant" said about salt,
salt sweetens the meat,
so too with the "covenant" said about suffering,

phrases.aramaic: יִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: sufferings scrub away all of a person's sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that ריש לקיש's teaching expresses the same idea as the קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suffering, called a 'covenant' like salt, cleanses all of a person's sins, just as salt sweetens meat.

steps.title: Three gifts that come only through suffering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says ה׳ gave ישראל three good gifts, Torah, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא, and all of them came only through suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says, הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישראל three good gifts, and He gave all of them only through suffering. They are: תורה, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about suffering. It shows that suffering is the path to ה׳'s greatest gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the focus was on suffering cleansing sins. Here רבי שמעון בן יוחי adds that suffering is also what makes ישראל ready to receive Torah, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא. It opens a new line that the גמרא will go on to explain.
steps.whatToRemember: Suffering cleanses sin (the slave's tooth and eye, and salt), and suffering is the way to Torah, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
Three good gifts
the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to Israel,
and He did not give any of them
except through suffering.

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן: תּוֹרָה וְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: These are: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from suffering cleansing sins to suffering as the way to receive ה׳'s great gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא were given to ישראל only through suffering.

steps.title: Proof that Torah comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that תורה is acquired only through suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that תורה comes through suffering? Because the פסוק says: 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה׳, and from Your Torah You teach him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving the three gifts from Step 26, one at a time. First it proves that תורה comes through suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק are read as one idea. First ה׳ afflicts the person, and then He teaches him from His תורה. So the suffering leads to the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: You afflict him, You bring suffering on him

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק from Steps 22 and 23, where the גמרא read it differently. Here רבי שמעון בן יוחי uses it in its simple order: suffering comes first, and תורה follows.

phrases.english: Torah, from where do we know?
As it is said: 'Happy is the man
whom You afflict, ה׳,
and from Your Torah You teach him.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:12

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first of the three gifts listed by רבי שמעון בן יוחי in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That תורה is acquired only through suffering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 94:12, where affliction is followed by teaching from the תורה.

steps.title: Proof that ארץ ישראל comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from two nearby פסוקים in דברים that ארץ ישראל comes after ה׳ disciplines us.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל: as it is written, 'Just as a man disciplines his son, ה׳ your God disciplines you.' And right after that it is written, 'For ה׳ your God is bringing you to a good land.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא proves the second gift, ארץ ישראל. It shows that ארץ ישראל also comes through suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the order of the פסוקים. First the תורה speaks about ה׳ disciplining us like a father disciplines a son. Right after that it speaks about bringing us into the good land. The discipline comes first, and the land comes as a result.

keyTerms.meaning: A good land, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Eretz Yisrael, as it is written:
'Just as a man disciplines his son,
ה׳ your God disciplines you,'
phrases.notes: דברים 8:5

phrases.english: and it is written right after it:
'For ה׳ your God is bringing you
to a good land.'
phrases.notes: דברים 8:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of proofs and moves from the first gift to the second.
steps.raayaObject: That ארץ ישראל is acquired only through suffering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 8:5 and 8:7. The good land is mentioned right after ה׳'s discipline.

steps.title: Proof that the World to Come comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from משלי that עולם הבא, the 'way of life,' is reached through the rebukes of discipline.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולם הבא: as it is written, 'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light, and the way of life is the rebukes of discipline.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third and last gift, עולם הבא. This finishes the proofs for רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'way of life' is understood as the path to עולם הבא, the true life. The פסוק says this path is 'the rebukes of discipline,' meaning suffering. So a person reaches עולם הבא through suffering in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of life, read here as the path to עולם הבא
Rebukes of discipline, meaning suffering that corrects a person

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's three gifts are each proven from a פסוק. תורה comes from תהלים, ארץ ישראל from דברים, and עולם הבא from משלי. All three are reached through suffering.

phrases.english: The World to Come, as it is written:
'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light,
and the way of life is the rebukes of discipline.'
phrases.notes: משלי 6:23. The 'way of life' is read as the road to עולם הבא, and that road is suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and final proof, which completes the support for Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That עולם הבא is acquired only through suffering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 6:23. The 'way of life' is reached through 'rebukes of discipline.'

steps.title: A new teaching about Torah and kindness begins
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a new ברייתא before רבי יוחנן about someone who is busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who is busy with תורה and with acts of kindness...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching, a ברייתא recited in front of רבי יוחנן. This line only sets up the case of a person busy with תורה and kindness. The rest of the statement comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of suffering continues, but the focus now shifts to a specific kind of person. This person learns תורה and also does acts of kindness. What the ברייתא says about him comes in the next words, and רבי יוחנן will react to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא recited (a ברייתא) before him

phrases.english: A Tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is someone whose job was to memorize ברייתות and recite them out loud in the study hall.

phrases.english: Anyone who is busy with Torah
and with acts of kindness

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs of the three gifts, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the wider subject of suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up: a person who is busy with תורה and with acts of kindness. The ruling about him follows in the next words.
